Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

average adjective

ordinary, middling

also ordinary, middling, mediocre, of average height

classical

Mart. 1.16.1: sunt quaedam mediocria
Cic. Brut. 136: ōrātōrēs mediocrēs (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. normal, ordinary, average

mediocris, mediocre

adjective, third declension

average, middling, ordinary; mediocre

Between too much and too little (Lewis & Short): of size, ability or worth. With a negative it turns into praise, nōn mediocris, “considerable” (see significant).

Other words

  • modicus, modica, modicum — moderate, of middling size

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 275: average, modicus; Cic. Fam. 5.12.4: modicum quoddam corpus, a book of moderate size (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediocria, sunt mala plūra quae legis hīc: aliter nōn fit, Avīte, liber

    some of what you read here is good, some average, more of it bad: there’s no other way to make a book, AvitusMart. 1.16

  • statūrā prope jūstā esse

    to be of about average heightTraupman 327

See also normal, average, significant, so-so, medium.

SourcesLewis & Short: mediocris · Lewis & Short: modicus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. normal, ordinary, average.
